evals.prompt: The empty state on the Orders screen looks different from everywhere else. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the shared empty-state component, makes Orders use it, and checks every other screen for divergent copies instead of restyling Orders alone.
assertions: Searches for an existing shared empty-state component before editing
Orders uses the shared component rather than a restyled local copy
Checks other screens for divergent empty states and merges them
Introduces no new raw color, spacing, or radius values

evals.prompt: Here's the Figma for the new settings card: 18px padding, #7B32F8 accent, 14px radius. Build it.
evals.expected_output: The agent maps the values to the nearest existing tokens and reports where the design differs from the system instead of adding raw values or new near-duplicate tokens.
assertions: Uses existing spacing, color, and radius tokens
Does not add a near-duplicate token for a value close to an existing one
Reports where the design differs from the system
Reuses existing components for the card's controls

evals.prompt: The Save button grows when it shows its spinner and the row jumps. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The fix lives in the shared button component: the loader replaces content inside a fixed-size box, so every button stops jumping, not just this one.
assertions: Fixes the shared button component, not this screen only
The button keeps the same size while loading
The spinner replaces the label inside the same box

evals.prompt: The filter icon on the Feed screen is wrong: it's a funnel, and it should be the sliders icon from our icon set. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent swaps the icon at its shared source or searches every use of the filter icon, so the Feed, Discovery, and any other filter control all show the same sliders icon from the one icon set, at the same stroke weight and scale size.
assertions: Searches the codebase for every use of the filter icon, not only the Feed screen
Every filter control ends up with the same icon, changed at a shared source or at each use
The icon comes from the project's existing icon set, not a new library, an SVG copy, or an emoji
Icon size and stroke come from the existing scale rather than raw values
The response lists the screens that changed

evals.prompt: In dark mode the text inputs disappear: when focused, their background matches the screen background. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The fix is in the input's surface tokens: a dark-mode pair that keeps the input distinct from its container in every state (default, focus, disabled, error). The shared input component uses those tokens and every screen with inputs is checked, with no per-screen color overrides.
assertions: The fix changes theme tokens or the shared input component, not a single screen
The input background stays visibly distinct from its container in dark mode in default, focus, disabled, and error states
Light mode is checked too and stays distinct
No raw hex values are added to screens to patch the problem
Other screens that use inputs are checked and reported

evals.prompt: On the landing page the clients block separates items with dots ('Fintech · Mobile · 2025'). Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent drops the dots for a separation the system already uses (a gap, color, or background suited to this block), applies it through a shared component or style, and moves every other dot-separated list to it.
assertions: Removes the dot separators
Separates items with a gap, color, or background rather than slashes or another glyph
Uses or creates one shared separator style rather than editing this block alone
Searches for other dot-separated lists and moves them to the shared style
Adds no spacing or color values outside the tokens

evals.prompt: On the iPad and on touch laptops our cards stay highlighted after a tap. Hover styles are enabled with an isDesktop check. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent removes the device-type check and gates hover styles by capability with (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), in the shared card or a shared hover utility, so taps never leave a sticky hover anywhere, and lists the components it changed.
assertions: Removes the device-type or user-agent check that enables hover
Gates hover styles with (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) or the platform equivalent
The fix lives in a shared component, utility, or token layer rather than one screen
Mouse hover on a fine-pointer device still works
Lists every component or screen that used the old check
